title: Proteomic characterization of synaptosomes and sarkosyl-insoluble protein inclusions from Alzheimer's disease patients
projectDescription: Alzheimer’s disease is characterized by neuropathological accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles composed of amyloid-beta peptides and hyperphosphorylated tau protein, respectively. These neuropathological changes alter the function of neurons, including synaptic contacts between interacting neurons, eventually resulting in neuronal dysfunction and neurodegeneration. Here, we simultaneously isolated nerve terminals (synaptosomes) and larger sarkosyl-insoluble protein inclusions from postmortem brains from Alzheimer’s disease and control cases and performed proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses.
sampleProcessingProtocol: From homogenates of postmortem brain tissue samples, insoluble protein inclusions were isolated based on their differential solubility in the detergent sarkosyl, whereas synaptosomes were isolated on discontinuous Percoll gradients. The proteins in the resulting fractions were reduced, alkylated and digested using Lys-C and trypsin (sarkosyl-insoluble fraction) or trypsin (synaptosomal fraction). Peptides for data-dependent acquisition were additionally labelled with TMT 10-plex (sarkosyl-insoluble fraction) or TMT 11-plex (synaptosomal fraction) followed by enrichment of phosphopeptides and off-line fractionation of both non-modified peptide and phosphopeptide samples by high pH reversed-phase separation. A subset of the non-modified peptide sample from the sarkosyl-insoluble fraction was also off-line fractionated using isoelectric focusing. All samples were analyzed by nano-LC-MS/MS.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files from data-dependent acquisition were processed using Proteome Discoverer (v2.5, Thermo Fisher Scientific). An in-house Mascot server was used to search the mass spectra against the human Swiss-Prot database using the following settings: precursor mass tolerance of 10 ppm, fragment mass tolerance of 0.05 Da, and a maximum of 2 missed cleavages for trypsin. All database searches were performed with carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues (C) and TMT6plex on lysine (K) residues and the peptide N-terminus (N-term) as fixed modifications. For the non-modified data, oxidation of methionine (M) was included as a dynamic modification, whereas phosphorylation of serine (S), threonine (T) or tyrosine (Y) residues were included as a dynamic modification in the phosphopeptide data. For the non-modified data, an additional database search was performed with semi-trypsin set as enzyme (maximum 2 missed cleavages allowed). The identified peptides/proteins were filtered against a 1% FDR cut-off, and only proteins with at least 2 unique peptides identified were considered for further analysis in the non-modified data. Raw data files from data-independent acquisition were processed using Spectronaut (v15.2, Biognosys). Database searches were performed using default BGS factory settings and mass spectra were searched against a sample-specific hybrid library for the sarkosyl-insoluble fraction and the synaptosomal fraction, respectively. The identified proteins were filtered against a 1% FDR cut-off, and only proteins identified with more than 1 peptide were considered for further analysis.
